text: A 42-year-old woman presents with six weeks of pain, swelling and morning stiffness in the small joints of both hands. Examination shows synovitis of several MCP joints. Bloods show a normal CRP. Plan: urgent referral to rheumatology, request rheumatoid factor.

A 19-year-old woman, not pregnant, reports three days of dysuria and suprapubic discomfort with no fever or flank pain. Diagnosis: uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection. Plan: three-day course of first-line antibiotic, fluids and simple analgesia, return if not settling in 48 hours.

Recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches with nausea and photophobia, two or three a month, disabling for a day each time. Neurological examination normal. Plan: triptan with an anti-inflammatory for attacks, discuss a preventive, start a headache diary.

A 68-year-old woman with a flare of inflammatory joint disease is started on long-term oral glucocorticoids at a high dose. She has a history of a wrist fracture after a fall. Plan: bone protection now, fracture risk assessment.
No headache, no visual disturbance, no neurological symptoms. Presents with a two-day history of dysuria and frequency. Not pregnant. Plan: back-up antibiotic prescription and self-care advice.
Minutes of the finance committee. The chair opened the meeting at 10:00. The quarterly budget was approved with one amendment to the travel line. Next meeting in six weeks.
